answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may influence shared decisions, with voting weight capped per bond and bonds slashed when identities are proven to coordinate fraudulently. One attacker can still create many accounts, but each must lock real capital, and splitting a fixed budget does not multiply its voting power. This makes a sybil swarm costly rather than impossible: a shale-backed grove of accounts may look broad, yet a gale of coordinated abuse risks forfeiting the bonds.
